78.t: Arranging for Barnet again; Ford Leary's laryngitis before the Paramount
78.s: In 1943-44 Horace wrote for Charlie Barnet, whose band had Billy May and Cliff Leeman. When trombonist-singer Ford Leary lost his voice before a Paramount booking, Barnet sent Horace to Harlem to find a singer.
78.ch: Army band, Lena Horne, Billie Holiday and the 1950s
78.q: Yes. Along that era, I believe I was doing quite a bit of arranging for Charley Barnet and his great band, you know, and Billy May was in that band, the great arranger and trumpet player. Course Charley had some great guys that could play, and of course, I think that Cliff Leeman, drum --

78.t: Backing Lena Horne with a small band at the Capitol Theatre
78.s: At Chez Paris and the Capitol with Xavier Cugat on the bill, Horace assembled Sid Catlett, Billy Taylor, Al Casey, Dick Vance, Benny Morton, Buddy Bostic and Edmond Hall at about $3,000 a week, paid by MGM.
78.ch: Army band, Lena Horne, Billie Holiday and the 1950s
78.q: She was a princess. We played the Chez Paris in Chicago, and I got a group together to back her, and (unintelligible) was terrific. And then we began to rehearse to go into an MGM House, the Capitol Theatre in New York City, and Xavier Cugat, Robert Walker, and Lena Horne on the same bill.

78.t: Lena Horne asks him to be her pianist and arranger
78.s: Staying at Juan Tizol's house, Horace met Lena Horne again through Rose Tizol; she offered him a tour of RKO theatres and Chez Paris and paid far more than he'd have asked.
78.ch: Army band, Lena Horne, Billie Holiday and the 1950s
78.q: Well, Willie Best had that apartment, and we used to talk. Well anyway, Lena came over to visit Juan Tizol's wife, Rose, one day, and I was in the house

78.t: Lena Horne years: scores, recordings, Nellie Lutcher, three months' advance pay
78.s: He stayed almost four years, supervising her recordings (Sid Catlett suggested Nellie Lutcher as pianist) and received three months' advance pay while she married Lennie Hayton and traveled.
78.ch: Army band, Lena Horne, Billie Holiday and the 1950s
78.q: So I had to check my head, you know. It wouldn't come out. So man, it was a lovely thing, and I made a lot of scores for her, and she paid me for all of them. I supervised her recordings, and on one of the sessions, guess who I had playing piano for me, and I was the conductor? Nellie Letcher.

78.t: Catlett's $500 fee, Nellie Lutcher on the Lena Horne date, and Dave Barbour
78.s: At the Capitol Theatre run with Lena, Catlett got $500 a week and recommended his wife Nellie Lutcher as pianist for the recording session; Dave Barbour helped pick non-studio musicians.
78.ch: Portraits from Hemphill to Getz, and the bebop question
78.q: Another time I had the pleasure of using Big Syd Catlett was Lena Horn on this Capital. He was playing -- you know, I should name that eight pieces the -- I can't think of a good name to describe that, the eight millionaires for those weeks, 'cause this is the money they got. In fact, --

78.t: Finding Lena Horne for Charlie Barnet at the Valencia and Paramount
78.s: Horace tracks Lena Horne down at Harlem's Regent Theatre and brings her to the Bronx to sing with Barnet; she buys a gown, breaks it up, and goes on to the Paramount. Barnet bets on horses, and Horace later toured with Lena.
78.ch: Army band, Lena Horne, Billie Holiday and the 1950s
78.q: MR. HENDERSON: Lena Horne. She had just come in from Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania having been divorced from her husband, so there's a little theatre in New York City -- there was, I don't know if there is now or not -- called the Regent at 116th and Seventh Avenue. So I went back stage in the Apollo…

105.t: Eight years with Lena Horne and mentor Lennie Hayton
105.s: Playing for singers, learning from Hayton, Luther Henderson and Strayhorn, and being a professional.
105.q: No it’s not. But if you think in terms of being a professional, hey, you can get just like a doctor, a lawyer or anybody else. You are a professional musician.

105.t: Eight years with Lena Horne: show business and playing behind her
105.s: Lena's husband Lenny Hayton taught him chess and cognac, his life turned toward show business, he missed one gig in eight years, and he describes how he sat behind her and her unpredictability.
105.q: So the next rehearsal all of a sudden man, here’s Lena Horne. We meet and this little guy turned out to be Lenny Hayton.

105.t: House drummer at Billy Berg's and the audition for Lena Horne
105.s: He became house drummer at Billy Berg's and was called to audition for Lena Horne at Luther Henderson's with bassist Charlie Drayton, rehearsing for ten days before being hired at $125 a week.
105.q: I was the house band. Every now and then -- the rhythm section -- you know, every time somebody came in, that’s how I played for Lady, (unintelligible). In the meantime I get a call one afternoon and they said, would you make an audition for Lena Horne. I didn’t even know who Lena Horne was, man.

230.t: How Lena Horne joined the band at the Casino Theater
230.s: With his singers hoarse, Barnet asked the Apollo's Clarence Robinson for help and Lena Horne was fetched from a movie; she stayed about nine months.
230.ch: Sidemen, mixed bands, the Apollo and Lena Horne
230.q: Well, Lena came to us under a distressed circumstances on our part, and strangely enough through the Apollo. We were playing a two day theater up in the Bronx

230.t: Lena Horne leaves the band after outshining Dinah Shore at the Paramount
230.s: Dinah Shore demanded Horne be removed from the Paramount bill, and Barnet released her from her 125 dollar a week contract; Cafe Society followed.
230.ch: Sidemen, mixed bands, the Apollo and Lena Horne
230.q: Yeah, it was murder. Of course then when she left the band that was quite a story too. She was my singer, we went in the Paramount, and Dinah Shore was the headline act, and of course as the band singer in the Paramount you always played an opening number, and then your girl singer came on. Well,…

412.t: The Village Vanguard: Lion of Trinidad and Pearl Bailey
412.s: Hodes played the Vanguard with Max Kaminsky and Wild Bill Davison and heard the Lion of Trinidad. He recalls Pearl Bailey and Max Gordon, who later paid her $1500 for the same act.
412.ch: Jam sessions, pay and the Vanguard (retyped)
412.q: This is how impressed you get, when you make the New York scene. That's it. So these were the early struggles in New York, until you start getting a few other breaks. Village Vanguard was a break. You go in there with your own trio, and I went in there with Max Kaminsky and Freddy , and then I came…

412.t: The Village Vanguard: Lion of Trinidad and Pearl Bailey
412.s: Hodes played the Vanguard with Max Kaminsky and Wild Bill Davison and heard the Lion of Trinidad. He recalls Pearl Bailey and Max Gordon, who later paid her $1500 for the same act.
412.ch: Jam sessions, pay and the Vanguard (corrected typing)
412.q: This is how impressed you get, when you make the New York scene. That's it. So these were the early struggles in New York, until you start getting a few other breaks. Village Vanguard was a break. You go in there with your own trio, and I went in there with Max Kaminsky and Freddy Moore and then I…

115.s: George Duvivier called him for Lena Horne's trio; Lennie Hayton, her husband, did arrangements and played piano.
115.q: What's his name? I can never think of this guy's name. I always have to ask George Devivier what his name is.

115.t: Anxiety on the Lena Horne job and leaving at the Cocoanut Grove
115.s: He read her snarling vocal style as aimed at him, grew so tense a doctor found high blood pressure, and gave notice in Los Angeles.
115.q: Not with the trio. The only thing that got me with her, it was little things she would do, kind of snarl in her singing, and I thought she was snarling at me. But she wasn't, at all. It was just the way she put her song over. And that used to worry me. I was thinking, maybe I did something wrong,…

653.t: Patsy at the Dew Drop and the blues singers of the day
653.s: The blues singers of the era and the performer Patsy, who chose to be announced as man or woman at the Dew Drop.
653.q: I can't think of Tip-A-Lite's name now. Uh-huh. But anyhow, he sang the blues. In those days, the blues singers was Tip-A-Lite, Joe August, who was named Google Eyes, Roy Brown, Fats Domino was just getting started. Um, Lloyd Ignatius, um, um, Patsy Vildar was the toast of the town. Yeah, sure.…

321.s: He got the Liza Minnelli gig as a late call on Lawrence Feldman's recommendation, and handles keys and her spontaneity.
321.q: You know. When I got the gig with Liza Minelli for a while, which is 1979, which I was definitely the 15th call or something because they had asked Lawrence Feldman my friend. They got to the saxophones to ask about piano players. And so Lawrence Feldman recommended me. So you know when a saxophone…

759.t: Lena Horne, Gerry Mulligan and Basie's fixed arrangements
759.s: He worked with Lena Horne and Mulligan, who kept changing things, unlike Basie whose arrangements stayed settled.
759.q: Yeah, it sure did. But working with Brubeck and the whole Brubeck clan was just absolutely delightful. And then, after that, it’s been very notable. I’ve worked off and on for a few years with Lena Horne, who is one of my favorite all-time people in the world, not only just as an entertainer, but…

122.t: Hines on the road; backing Flip Phillips, Getz and singers with Vernon Alley
122.s: Hines handled the road details; with Alley he backed Flip Phillips, Stan Getz, Arthur Prysock and Dorothy Dandridge.
122.q: So I was just reading somebody’s book — his book — and it was talking about that band and what a great band it was. He said Jesus, everybody in there was full of arrangers and everybody was gung ho and everybody could play, and all he had to do — he had to learn as a matter of fact. But his mind…

16.t: Opening a studio and joining Lena Horne
16.s: After the Navy he opened a studio; Ellington and Strayhorn recommended him to Lena Horne and he worked with her for about three years, then coached singers and wrote for Eartha Kitt.
16.q: Yes. What happened was that when I came out of the Navy, I decided that I would open a studio. I had ?? and she had a studio bass player by the name of Doles Dickens and do writing, you know write for special material and for singers and stuff like that and coaching. And it was during that time…

1.t: Margie, Mary Stafford and Jazzbo, the two-voiced singer
1.s: Danny recalls blues singer Mary Stafford, buxom Margie, and little Jazzbo who sang soprano and baritone in the cabaret ups.
1.ch: Arriving in New York: the Nest Club and Harlem nightlife
1.q: All right. Now, there was Margie Sith(?). Later on there was Mary Stafford. You'll see her name on some records. She made a few records during that time.

67.s: Cheatham knew Mattie Hite at the Bellman's Club, where she sang risque songs from table to table.
67.ch: Chicago clubs, entertainers and tent shows
67.q: And she would keep the band playing for maybe a couple of hours. Once -- during one song. And she had a lot of -- most of her songs were very risqué. And she'd pick up a lot of money, you know, going from table to table singing these risqué type of songs.

166.t: The Three Deuces quartet with Pearl Bailey and Ann Robinson
166.s: On 52nd Street he played with singers Pearl Bailey, Willie Dukes and scat singer Ann Robinson.
166.ch: Records, Blanton, the Chicago scene, Nat Cole and Nadine
166.q: could sing was 'St. Louis Blues.' She was getting 35 dollars a week. And they had a gay young man called Willie Dukes sing Honeysuckle Rose, honey, suck my nose, and Peewee Marquette, you know he couldn't sing.

89.t: How the Liza act was built and hiding Fats from alimony collectors
89.s: The female singer was the glamour of such acts while the band was his; Fats had to be hidden on arrival in towns because of unpaid alimony.
89.q: But we had hired her to sing, but you have to have a feature attraction in a vaudeville act. You have a center. The act was built around her, you see, and -- as a singer, and she did a little dance and she was the glamour of the act, you see. Five big rough men in tuxedos and all, but she was the…

566.t: The Village Vanguard with Eddie Heywood, and Pearl Bailey as her fill-in
566.s: At the Vanguard with Eddie Heywood, she went home for Derby time and found Pearl Bailey to cover. Pearl got her big break at the Blue Angel and also worked briefly for Basie.
566.ch: After Basie: Cafe Society to Los Angeles
566.q: Oh, he was super-duper, yes indeed. I went down there and I stayed and stayed and it was getting Derby (Kentucky) time. So I had to go home for the Derby, you know.

389.t: Artie Shaw's new band: Lena Horne record and Lips Page arrangements
389.s: Shaw's lawyer called him to write for the new band; they made a Lena Horne record and he arranged Blues in the Night before Shaw joined the Navy.
389.ch: Freelance and studio work in New York
389.q: He was putting together a new band. His lawyer called me up. What was his name? Andy Weinberg. He called up and he said, "Artie's getting this band together, and he would like you to give him a call." So we got together, we went down and made a record before we got the band together, we went down…

75.s: He played for Gladys Lundy, a masculine-dressed singer of spicy special material who later turned religious.
75.ch: The war years: Barnet, Hot Lips Page, Newton and Kirby
75.q: : Well, when I heard him play, and the more I listened to him, the more I stayed, and I forgot about the axe...the more interested I became in playing the axe/acts(?), and not trying to outplay him, because...

239.t: Lenny Hayton and handling Lena Horne's act
239.s: Jones replaced Lenny Hayton as Lena Horne's conductor and learned discipline tricks from him at the Waldorf.
239.q: That's right. I'll tell you, the only other man that I learned -- well, several people I've learned a lot from -- was Lenny Hayton, Lena Horne's husband.
